why: B is false (not_B): its clause (2) 'if the index is finite it is attained' quantifies over arbitrary SETS A ⊆ V; for A = ∅ the index (empty supremum) is 0 but no subspace lies in ∅. Hence A ⇒ B is false and B ⇒ A holds vacuously (ex falso). With A a subspace (B_sub) the statement holds outright (B_sub_holds: the zero subspace is admissible, a bounded nonempty family in ℕ∞ attains its sup; the nullity clause is span ≠ ⊥). The notions agree: Morse.IsNegDefOn = IsNegDefSub (Iff.rfl) and bIndex univ H = Morse.formIndex H for bilinear H (bIndex_univ_eq_formIndex), so A's le_formIndex ⇔ B_sub's first clause on univ (both proved, #rt_check OK). Corrected, the two are incomparable: A has monotonicity under form-preserving maps and formIndex = sigNeg in finite dimension; B has attainment and the nullity clause (no nullity notion in this item of the project) and allows non-bilinear H on subspaces.
B_issue: Clause (2) (finite index attained) is stated for every set A ⊆ V and is false when 0 ∉ A (e.g. A = ∅). Milnor's A = TΩ_γ is a vector space; with A a subspace (indeed whenever 0 ∈ A) the clause holds.
